subject: Post-incident briefing: service recovery, timeline and commitments
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident briefing: service recovery, timeline and commitments

Hi Jia and Marco —

First, thank you for your patience during this morning's incident. We know any disruption to inference is costly for Wavenet and appreciate you working with us while we investigated. Attached is an initial RCA draft (wavenet_rca_v1.pdf) and a remediation tracker (remediation_plan.xlsx).

High-level summary:
- Impact window: 2027-04-11 07:48–08:56 PT — degraded throughput for inference requests and intermittent timeouts for a subset of customer traffic routed through our eu-west-1 edge.
- Root cause (summary): a cache invalidation race in the routing layer combined with a stale failover mapping that caused a small fraction of requests to be repeatedly retried to a misconfigured backend.
- Mitigation executed: traffic cutover and hotfix deployed (08:55 PT), automated fallback tightened, slow path throttles adjusted.

Requested next steps from us:
1) Confirm complete timeline and a technical appendix for your security and compliance team (we've included timeline.csv).
2) Provide concrete remediation owners and ETAs (see remediation_plan.xlsx).
3) Schedule a 30-minute runbook review to walk through the fixes and the verification plan.

I'll follow up with a more detailed technical note from Diego and Jonas. We're committed to a post-incident review with your engineering and security leads this week.

Apologies again — Laura

--

- Do you have an ETA on the permanent fix and how it will be validated across regions?
- Can you confirm which customer CIDRs were affected (we logged a drop in production between 07:55 and 08:10 PT)?

If you can share the timeline and a short statement about data access, I can loop in our security compliance folks. We can do the runbook review tomorrow morning if that works.

Subject: Re: Post-incident briefing: service recovery, timeline and commitments

Jia — quick technical timeline and answers below. Happy to expand during the call.

Timeline (detailed):
- 07:47 PT — first elevated error rate observed by canary monitors in our eu-west-1 edge cluster.
- 07:55 PT — retries increased; we saw a spike in 502/504 from a small subset of backends.
- 08:12 PT — alerted on routing anomalies; initial mitigation: drain a small set of backend nodes.
- 08:31 PT — identified stale failover mapping entry for the affected shard that caused repeated retries into a misconfigured backend.
- 08:42 PT — manual configuration removed; further errors persisted due to cache race on invalidation.
- 08:55 PT — hotfix (short-circuit on stale mapping + safe re-prime of cache) rolled to the affected edge and traffic normalized by 08:56 PT.

Data exposure statement: we have no evidence that payloads were exfiltrated or persisted outside of normal request logging. The failure resulted in extra retries and transient timeouts; logs show repeated attempts but no anomalous downstream writes. We'll provide the audit log slice for your security team (see timeline.csv).

Permanent fix & validation plan:
- Short term (this week): harden cache invalidation paths and add circuit breakers for mapping anomalies (owner: Jonas Weber, ETA: 2027-04-18).
- Medium term (30 days): automated integration tests that simulate invalid mapping race conditions and per-region canary gating (owner: Diego Fernandez, ETA: 2027-05-11).
- Verification: we've added a post-deploy synthetic that mimics Wavenet traffic patterns; we'll share weekly validation reports for four weeks.

Attachments: timeline.csv (detailed timestamps + log excerpts).

Diego

Subject: Re: Post-incident briefing: service recovery, timeline and commitments

Jia — adding the runtime/serving detail.

Root cause (technical): the routing layer maintains a per-shard failover mapping in a distributed cache. When a mapping update coincided with an asynchronous invalidation, one cache partition returned a stale mapping that pointed to a backend which had an outdated config. The serving runtime's retryer interpreted repeated errors as transient and retried aggressively, amplifying the traffic to the stale backend.

What we changed immediately:
- Hotfix: short-circuit retries when mapped backend fails a healthcheck, skip stale mapping re-use (rolled 08:55 PT).
- Failover mapping validation: added a checksum-based verification of mapping entries to prevent re-using inconsistent state during re-primes.

Planned mitigations (owner + ETA):
- Automated mapping verification on write paths (Jonas Weber) — ETA 2027-04-18.
- Retry policy tuning per-client (config flag rollout, incremental) — ETA 2027-04-25.

I attached the minimal diff applied during the hotfix for your review (hotfix-diff.patch). Happy to walk through the code path on the call.

Jonas

- Implement mapping verification on write paths (owner: Jonas Weber) — ETA: 2027-04-18.
- Add per-client retry gating and canary checks to prevent amplification (owner: Diego Fernandez) — ETA: 2027-04-25.
- Weekly validation report for four weeks (owner: Diego Fernandez) — first report by 2027-04-19.

Laura
